newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Second Australian charged in Briton's murder.
newsitem.headline: Second Australian charged in Briton's murder.

text.p: A 22-year-old Australian man was charged on Wednesday as an accessary to the bashing murder of British tourist Brian Hagland at Sydney's Bondi Beach 11 days ago, police said.

Sean Cushman, a resident of Bondi, was released on A$10,000 (US$7,900) bail after becoming the second man charged over Hagland's murder. Cushman must report to police daily before he appears again in court on November 1.
Cushman did not formally enter a plea, but his lawyer told the Waverley Magistrates Court that Cushman would defend the charge "vigorously".

Aaron Martin, 22, of nearby Rushcutters Bay, sobbed on Tuesday as he was charged with the murder of Hagland. Martin did not seek bail or enter a plea before being remanded in custody to appear again on November 1.
Hagland, a 28-year-old London postman, died from head and internal injuries after being assaulted in a street attack witnessed by his fiancee in the early hours of Saturday, September 7.
His fiancee, Connie Casey, 25, has said two men kicked and punched Hagland to death in an unprovoked attack near Australia's most famous beach.
Martin voluntarily walked into the Bondi Beach police station last week to assist police with their investigation. He was charged after returning for a second interview.
The prosecutor in Martin's case told the court that it would take a month to prepare the case, which would involve 34 witnesses.
Casey and Hagland had been in Australia for eight months and had been due to visit New Zealand before returning to Britain to be married.
